inlines.v: INTERCOM'MON, verb intransitive [inter and common.] 1. To feet at the same table. 2. To graze cattle in a common pasture; to use a common with others, or to possess or enjoy the right of feeding in common. Common because of vicinage, is where the inhabitants of two townships contiguous to each other, have usually intercommoned with one another.
